name: Daylite
tagline: A Mac-native CRM that glues contacts, projects, pipelines and Apple Mail into one shared database for small teams.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is not exotic: people, companies, projects, opportunities, tasks, notes, and a pile of links between them. An agent can absolutely produce a local single-user CRM that holds all of that and runs fine on one laptop in a session or two. What it cannot produce in one shot is the part people actually buy: a real Mac app, an iPhone app, offline-capable sync between them, and the Apple Mail plugin that files a thread against the right contact without you thinking about it. If you are a solo operator who lives in one browser window, the DIY build is genuinely enough. If you use Daylite because it is native and because your assistant sees the same records, this is a downgrade with extra chores.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app with a SQLite database where you track contacts, companies, projects and deals, attach notes and tasks to any of them, and see one merged timeline per record.
requirements: vCard or CSV export from your current contacts to seed the database
Willingness to log email manually or paste threads in as notes
whatYouLose: The Apple Mail integration: filing threads to contacts and projects from inside Mail is the whole reason many people tolerate Daylite
Native Mac and iOS apps with offline access and sync, instead of one browser tab on one computer
Multi-user sharing with permissions, delegation and a shared calendar
Two-way sync with Apple Calendar and Contacts, so your phone stops knowing anything
Activity sets, pipelines with saved stages and the other accumulated workflow furniture you did not realize you used
moatNotes: The moat is Apple-shaped: a Mail plugin, native clients and calendar sync are all things a one-shot build will not touch.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because CRM value is mostly capture friction, not schema. Daylite wins when the email you just answered becomes a logged interaction with two clicks inside Mail, and when your business partner opens the same project on an iPad an hour later. A local web CRM has no path to either without a real Mac app and a sync backend, which is a multi-week project, not a session. Solo users with low email volume can escape; two-person shops running their whole client pipeline through it generally cannot.
notes: Great first build for learning why relationship data is easy and relationship capture is not.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal CRM that runs entirely on my machine. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Node 20, TypeScript, Fastify for the API
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/crm.db, WAL mode
- React + Vite + Tailwind for the UI, served by Fastify in production
- Zod for validation, no ORM, hand-written SQL in a small data layer
- Any secrets go in .env, and there should be none needed for the core app

Data model:
- people: name, emails (many), phones (many), company_id, role, tags, notes field
- companies: name, domain, tags
- projects: name, status (open, on hold, done), company_id, due date
- deals: name, company_id, stage (lead, qualified, proposal, won, lost), amount, close date
- tasks: title, due date, done flag, polymorphic link to person, company, project or deal
- interactions: date, channel (email, call, meeting, note), body text, links to any number of people plus one optional project or deal
- generic link table so any record can be attached to any other

Features in scope:
- CRUD for every entity with keyboard-first forms
- One record page per person, company, project and deal showing a single merged timeline of interactions and tasks, newest first
- Global search across names, emails, tags and interaction bodies using SQLite FTS5
- A today view: tasks due or overdue, plus people with no interaction in 60 days
- Kanban board for deals by stage with drag between columns
- vCard and CSV import to seed people and companies, dedupe on email
- Paste-an-email-thread box that creates an interaction and auto-links people whose email addresses appear in the text
- Full JSON export of the whole database from one button

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- Mail client plugins, IMAP polling, calendar sync, mobile apps, multi-user auth, sharing or permissions

Deliverables: npm run dev for the app, a seed script with 20 fake records, a README explaining the schema and how to back up the SQLite file, and Vitest coverage on the link table and dedupe logic.
